newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 20,000 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 43.470 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in France received 15,000 tonnes and in Denmark 5,000 tonnes, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.797 million tonnes. This compares with the 53,750 tonnes awarded on April 17, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 1.944 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to end-September to be 43.470 Ecus per 100 kilos.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 30,000 and 40,000 tonnes versus 42,600 last week when the restitution was 43.737 Ecus.
